briefs.headline: No. 22 WVU host No. 23 Penn State in Morgantown
briefs.summary: Thursday, 7 p.m. at Dick Dlesk. The Mountaineers opened 2-0 over Dayton; Penn State drew 2-2 with then-No. 2 Notre Dame and have won the last six meetings.

briefs.headline: Reds answer St. Louis 5-4 with late runs
briefs.summary: Cincinnati scored in the sixth and eighth. Sam Moll went to 2-7 for the win, Matthew Liberatore fell to 5-11 and Emilio Pagan took his 16th save.

briefs.headline: Pirates hold off Detroit 4-3 at home
briefs.summary: Mason Montgomery went to 5-3 for the win and Kenley Jansen took the loss at 3-5. Pittsburgh are 5-5 over their last 10 and travel to the Dodgers on Friday.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Washington and the White Sox pitch shutouts
briefs.summary: The Nationals beat Texas 6-0 behind Cade Cavalli and the White Sox took the crosstown game from the Cubs 3-0. Arizona and the Dodgers both went 10 innings.

briefs.headline: Nashville lead the Eastern Conference on 46 points
briefs.summary: From 20 matches, at 14-4-2 and plus-25 on goal difference. FC Cincinnati are the closest followed club in fifth; Columbus sit 12th on a minus-5 difference.

briefs.headline: Aki basho is 24 days out and still unconfirmed
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association's English pages carry no September schedule, only that every day is sold out. A Sept. 13 opening in Tokyo is derived from the second-Sunday rule; the banzuke, the rankings sheet, is due Aug. 31.

sections.note: Sumo got its own search again. The Sept. 13-27 dates at Ryogoku Kokugikan are still carried only by ticket resellers, travel sites and fan databases, which this paper does not cite - a seventh straight morning. The Aug. 31 banzuke release is the moment Kyodo, NHK or the Japan Times must print them.

coming_in.item: The gun bear season opens Aug. 29 in SELECTED COUNTIES only, and the county list is not in the pamphlet's summary table, so no county is named here. Daily 1, possession 2, season limit 2; bag limits vary by county and permit class and sit on pamphlet pages 33-39.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: The recreational flounder season opens 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 and closes 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14 in coastal and joint waters under proclamation FF-27-2026, one fish per person per day at a 15-inch minimum, hook and line and gig only. Every fish kept must be reported to the division.

prime.item: Coastal waters: 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day. It is unlawful to possess a red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff one.
Coastal waters: 14 to 20 inches total length, three per day, of which one may exceed 26 inches.
Coastal waters: 14-inch minimum total length, five per day. The limits page is the one effective July 1, 2026.
Open year round to hunting; additional regulations are on pamphlet page 6.

notes.item: Southern flounder is closed and unlawful to possess until the Sept. 1 opening. Topsail Sound is coastal water, so Marine Fisheries governs it and not the inland digest.

Dove, snipe, rail, goose and duck dates are in WVDNR's separate 2026-27 migratory bird publication and not in the hunting summary table, so no migratory date is printed here. HIP registration is required. Deer and bear bag limits are likewise not in the table.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.read: 451 cfs - pushy. Wadeable at the edges, not across.
waters.working: Down from 1270 cfs a day ago and dropping steadily, so the river is coming back into itself rather than blown out. At this height it is a heavy-nymph-on-the-seam problem, not a long-leader one: a weighted stonefly or a sculpin pattern along the undercut banks and the soft edges, and stay out of the main current.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.9 ft and falling - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down five feet on the day and back to pool, which puts the fish on structure again. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait across the wing dams and the riprap is the first look, and the barge cuts hold fish once the colour clears.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 31.7 ft and falling - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Off three and a half feet from yesterday but still high and coloured. Debris is the hazard. The slack behind the lock wall and the rock is where to start, and a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the riprap is the second look after the swimbait.

waters.reading: Sound highs 2:30 AM at 3.1 ft and 3:07 PM at 3.9 ft at Hampstead; lows 8:46 AM at 0.6 ft and 9:45 PM at 1.2 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of the 3:07 PM high in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure. The afternoon high is the bigger of the two at 3.9 feet and the only one in daylight, so the push into it is the window. Mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet are the forage, so a soft plastic or live bait along the grass edges and the oyster bars while the water moves. Red drum and speckled trout are open; flounder is not.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and is the read that matters; the oceanfront station at Ocean City Beach pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - the Wrightsville Beach gauge returned none for a fourth morning.

sections.note: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at R.C. Byrd, and the Corps tailwater data is not reachable from this pipeline. The two gauges above are the ones that bracket the dam, and neither is the tailwater.

kicker: Every water in the paper is falling this morning; the Williams has come off 1270 cfs to 451 in a day.
